Therefore, the claim for carrying cost having not raised by the Petitioner in the Petition No. 221/MP/2021 is deemed to have been given up. 8. The Respondent, ERPC, was also directed to submit the reasons for not issuing the compensation statement attributable to the Petitioner, on account of the SCED for the period under dispute. In response, the Petitioner and Respondent ERPC have filed 12. The Commission, after hearing the parties at length on 18.11.2024, permitted the Petitioner and the Respondent WBSEDCL to file their written submissions. The Petitioner was also directed to file the following additional information, after serving a copy on the Respondents: 14. The Petitioner, in its written submissions dated 10.12.2024, and the Respondent 15. Based on the submission of the parties, the issues which emerge for consideration are the following: - (b) There is no delay attributable to the Respondent, as the compensation was duly paid in terms of the debit note dated 31.5.2023, issued by the Petitioner, and therefore, the question of restitution does not arise. The Petitioner's delay in raising the claim for carrying costs is a conscious decision and not an inadvertent error. In terms of Order II, Rule 2 of the CPC all the claims, arising out of the same cause of action, should have been included in the suit and the missed claims are to be considered as given up and cannot be claimed in a subsequent suit, and accordingly, the claim of carrying cost by the Petitioner, not raised in the Petition No. 221/MP/2023, is deemed to have been given up. considered view, the submissions of the Respondent are not acceptable. As regards the contention that the NTPC’s order dated 14.11.2023 is not applicable to the present case, it is pertinent to mention that Petition No. 221/MP/2021 was filed by the Petitioner, based on the ERPC advice to approach this Commission for seeking necessary clarification regarding the methodology of compensation for IPP stations, keeping in view that the share allocation of the Petitioner’s project is based on the fixed LTA quantum (in MW) to beneficiaries. Similar to the case of an NTPC Plant (CGS), whose allocation is done by the MOP, GOI (on a percentage basis), the Petitioner’s generating station (though an IPP) has long-term PPAs with the beneficiaries (on MW basis) and the tariff of the same is being determined by this Commission. ERPC has been issuing total compensation statements for CGS, including the SCED compensation recoverable from each beneficiary. The Petitioner’s generating station was included under SCED from 12.6.2019. In the above background and keeping in view the methodology adopted by the WRPC for IPPs of the Western Region, the Commission vide its order dated 12.1.2023 directed the ERPC to determine the beneficiary wise compensation due to part load operation including the consideration of the revised SHR of 2326.03 kcal/kWh, based on the tariff order dated 8.1.2022 in Petition No. 408/GT/2020 in respect of the Petitioner’s generating station. It is pertinent to mention that the Commission, vide its 4[th] Amendment dated 29.4.2016 to IEGC, introduced Regulation 6.3B viz Technical Minimum for operation of CGS/ISGS, whose tariff is determined by this Commission or adopted by this Commission. Thus, as decided in the case of NTPC, the compensation for the degradation of heat rate, in the present case, is based on the provisions of the Grid Code and the Tariff Regulations notified by this Commission. Even otherwise, we note that NTPC in its Petition (166/MP/2021) had not claimed any carrying cost, but the Commission, evidently, following the principles of restitution and time value of money and in terms of the provisions of the by the Petitioner arise from a different cause of action. In other words, Order II Rule 2 would not be applicable, where the second suit is based on a different and distinct cause of action. The contentions of the Respondent are therefore rejected. 32. Petition No. 67/MP/2024 is disposed of in terms of the above discussions and findings.
